lessons.name: Meet the Board
lessons.objective: Restore the starting position and make the first move for each side.
lessons.overview: Have the player replace three missing black pieces, replace three missing white pieces, then make one legal move for Black and one for White.

lessons.name: Making Captures
lessons.objective: Jump opposing pieces and learn which single captures are legal.
lessons.overview: Teach single forward captures by men: jump an adjacent opponent into the empty square beyond it, remove the captured piece, and distinguish blocked, friendly, backward, and king targets.

lessons.name: Capture Is Compulsory
lessons.objective: Learn that any available capture must be taken before an ordinary move.
lessons.overview: Teach compulsory captures across the board, free choice among legal single captures without rank priority, and why an unfavorable capture is still required.

lessons.name: Keep Jumping
lessons.objective: Follow a capture through every jump with the same piece.
lessons.overview: Teach complete multiple-jump sequences and choices between capture routes. Practice continuing with the same piece and recognizing when a sequence ends.

lessons.name: Becoming a King
lessons.objective: Reach the promotion row and learn when your turn ends.
lessons.overview: Explain the promotion row and that reaching it ends the turn, including during a capture. Guide pieces to promotion through ordinary moves and jumps.

lessons.name: Moving with Kings
lessons.objective: Use a king’s backward moves and captures to explore new routes.
lessons.overview: Teach one-square forward and backward movement, backward captures, and changing direction during multiple jumps. Compare legal moves for kings and uncrowned pieces.

lessons.name: How Games End
lessons.objective: Recognize wins, resignation, and drawn positions.
lessons.overview: Cover winning by capturing or immobilizing the opponent, resignation, and basic draw recognition. Classify finished positions and introduce Crown’s draw indicators.

lessons.name: Challenge: Your First Game
lessons.objective: Win a full guided match against Crown AI and review Unit 1.
lessons.overview: Play from the standard starting position as Black, with contextual guidance and an always-available Unit 1 rules reference. Beat beginner Crown AI, then finish the complete rules recap to complete the lesson. Retry after a loss or draw.

lessons.name: Spot the Threat
lessons.objective: Find the pieces your opponent could capture next turn.
lessons.overview: Identify pieces the opponent could capture on their next turn. Mark both the threatened piece and the landing square that makes the jump possible.

lessons.name: Before You Move
lessons.objective: Check whether moving one piece exposes another to capture.
lessons.overview: Show how moving one piece can expose another. Preview a candidate move and identify any new captures it permits.

lessons.name: Find a Safe Square
lessons.objective: Choose a legal destination that avoids an immediate material loss.
lessons.overview: Compare legal destinations for the same piece. Choose a destination that avoids an immediate material loss in the supplied position.

lessons.name: Protecting a Piece
lessons.objective: Protect your pieces through support and blocked jump destinations.
lessons.overview: Introduce support through recaptures and denying jump landing squares. Show why merely standing beside a friendly piece does not guarantee protection.

lessons.name: Count the Exchange
lessons.objective: Count each side’s losses through a capture and recapture.
lessons.overview: Follow a short capture-and-recapture sequence and count what each side loses. Distinguish equal exchanges from losing trades.

lessons.name: Beware the Second Jump
lessons.objective: See the full damage hidden behind an opponent’s first jump.
lessons.overview: Show how a seemingly harmless capture can become a multiple jump. Identify the full damage before deciding whether a move is safe.

lessons.name: The Safety Check
lessons.objective: Check forced captures, the opponent’s reply, and the resulting exchange.
lessons.overview: Combine the section into a repeatable routine: check compulsory captures, inspect the opponent’s reply, and count the resulting exchange. Apply it to mixed positions.

lessons.name: Challenge: Hold Your Ground
lessons.objective: Defend short positions without preventable material losses.
lessons.overview: Play short defensive positions and a brief continuation. Succeed by avoiding preventable material losses, rather than by defeating the opponent outright.

lessons.name: Make Them Jump
lessons.objective: Use compulsory captures to force a specific response.
lessons.overview: Introduce using compulsory captures to direct an opponent’s response. Choose a move that forces a specific capture when no alternative capture exists.

lessons.name: Give One, Take Two
lessons.objective: Offer one piece to force a reply that wins back more material.
lessons.overview: Teach a basic material-winning sacrifice. Offer one piece, follow the forced reply, and recover more material than was sacrificed.

lessons.name: Build a Multiple Jump
lessons.objective: Find the setup move that creates a multiple-jump capture.
lessons.overview: Arrange an opponent’s pieces into a capturable sequence. Find the setup move before executing the combination.

lessons.name: Remove the Defender
lessons.objective: Force away a supporting piece and exploit the weakness it leaves.
lessons.overview: Force away or exchange a piece that supports an opponent’s position. Exploit the weakness created after its removal.

lessons.name: Open the Landing Square
lessons.objective: Clear the landing square needed to make a capture possible.
lessons.overview: Teach that a blocked landing square can prevent a capture. Find a forcing sequence that clears the required square.

lessons.name: Choose Your Capture
lessons.objective: Compare capture routes by what happens after the jumps.
lessons.overview: Compare alternative legal capture routes by their consequences. Include examples where taking more immediately produces a worse result.

lessons.name: When the Sacrifice Fails
lessons.objective: Test a tempting sacrifice against alternative replies and recaptures.
lessons.overview: Examine tempting combinations that fail because of another legal reply or a final recapture. Separate sound sacrifices from hopeful ones.

lessons.name: Challenge: Find the Combination
lessons.objective: Find a sound setup and continuation in unfamiliar tactical positions.
lessons.overview: Solve unfamiliar positions mixing the section’s patterns. Require the setup and continuation, including recognizing a position where the apparent combination does not work.

lessons.name: Their Best Reply
lessons.objective: Find your opponent’s strongest reply to a proposed move.
lessons.overview: Replace “What do I want them to do?” with “What can they do?” Choose the opponent’s strongest immediate response to a proposed move.

lessons.name: Your Move, Their Move, Your Move
lessons.objective: Predict the squares and material balance three turns ahead.
lessons.overview: Calculate a three-turn sequence before moving. Predict the final squares and material balance, then play it out.

lessons.name: Find the Branches
lessons.objective: Spot where a forced sequence gives way to a choice of replies.
lessons.overview: Distinguish a forced sequence from one with alternatives. Identify the points where the opponent can choose a different reply.

lessons.name: Compare Two Plans
lessons.objective: Look ahead equally far to compare two candidate moves.
lessons.overview: Analyze two candidate moves using the same short lookahead. Compare the resulting material, safety, and promotion prospects.

lessons.name: Finish the Sequence
lessons.objective: Resolve the forced captures before judging an exchange.
lessons.overview: Avoid evaluating halfway through a capture exchange. Continue until immediate forced captures are resolved before judging the outcome.

lessons.name: Work Backward
lessons.objective: Work back from a desired capture or promotion to find its setup.
lessons.overview: Start from a desired capture or promotion and identify the arrangement needed to achieve it. Find a short sequence that creates that arrangement.

lessons.name: Calculate Without Moving
lessons.objective: Track a short sequence mentally and identify its final position.
lessons.overview: Gradually remove preview assistance. Track a short sequence mentally, then select or reconstruct its final position.

lessons.name: Challenge: Read Ahead
lessons.objective: Choose a move and predict the response with limited preview help.
lessons.overview: Solve mixed positions with limited preview support. Give the move and expected response; accept multiple sound solutions where appropriate.

lessons.name: Beyond the Piece Count
lessons.objective: Judge mobility, support, and promotion chances alongside material.
lessons.overview: Introduce mobility, support, and promotion prospects as additional ways to judge a position. Compare equal-material examples with visibly different strengths.

lessons.name: Stay Connected
lessons.objective: Improve coordination without creating an immediate tactical weakness.
lessons.overview: Explain how coordinated pieces can support exchanges and advances. Improve a fragmented position without creating an immediate tactical weakness.

lessons.name: Using the Center
lessons.objective: Develop useful central influence while keeping your pieces supported.
lessons.overview: Explore central influence and access to both sides of the board. Contrast useful central development with an unsupported advance.

lessons.name: Playing the Edges
lessons.objective: Weigh an edge route’s protection against its limited mobility.
lessons.overview: Examine the trade-off between fewer attacking approaches and fewer movement options. Choose between an edge route and a central route in contrasting positions.

lessons.name: Keep Your Options
lessons.objective: Preserve useful moves or restrict your opponent’s choices.
lessons.overview: Teach mobility and the danger of cramped formations. Select a move that preserves useful future moves or restricts the opponent.

lessons.name: Guarding the Back Row
lessons.objective: Decide when a back-row defender should stay or advance.
lessons.overview: Explain how back-row pieces can obstruct promotion and why holding them forever can also be costly. Decide when to retain or release a defender.

lessons.name: Trade with a Purpose
lessons.objective: Choose exchanges that improve your position or open a route forward.
lessons.overview: Evaluate exchanges that improve structure, remove a troublesome piece, or open a route forward. Compare the board before and after an equal trade.

lessons.name: Challenge: Improve Your Position
lessons.objective: Improve coordination, mobility, or promotion chances without conceding a tactic.
lessons.overview: Play several short scenarios with clear positional objectives. Assess whether the player improves mobility, coordination, or promotion prospects without conceding a tactic.

lessons.name: Find a Route to Crown
lessons.objective: Trace a promising promotion path and identify its obstacles.
lessons.overview: Trace possible promotion paths and identify obstacles. Select a promising route rather than simply advancing the nearest piece.

lessons.name: Escort the Runner
lessons.objective: Use supporting pieces to keep an advancing piece safe.
lessons.overview: Use supporting pieces to help an advancing piece survive. Choose an escort move that answers an interception threat.

lessons.name: Break Through
lessons.objective: Weigh the cost of an exchange or sacrifice that opens a promotion route.
lessons.overview: Use an exchange or sacrifice to open a promotion route. Compare the material cost with the resulting position.

lessons.name: Stop Their Promotion
lessons.objective: Intercept, block, or exchange an opposing runner before it crowns.
lessons.overview: Recognize an opposing runner and calculate an interception, block, or forced exchange. Solve defensive promotion problems.

lessons.name: Race to the Back Row
lessons.objective: Count the turns to promotion and decide whether to race or defend.
lessons.overview: Count turns to promotion while accounting for forced captures and interference. Decide whether to race or stop the opponent.

lessons.name: Activate Your King
lessons.objective: Bring your new king into useful play while avoiding traps.
lessons.overview: Bring a newly crowned king into useful play. Compare routes that improve its reach while avoiding traps and captures.

lessons.name: King and Piece Together
lessons.objective: Use a king to support an uncrowned piece’s advance.
lessons.overview: Coordinate a king with an uncrowned piece. Use the king to support an advance, remove an obstacle, or protect a promotion route.

lessons.name: Challenge: Earn the Crown
lessons.objective: Create and use a king, then stop an opposing promotion.
lessons.overview: Complete paired scenarios: create a king and use it effectively in one; prevent a dangerous opposing promotion in another.

lessons.name: Take Stock of the Ending
lessons.objective: Assess a sparse position and decide whether to convert or defend.
lessons.overview: Assess material, kings, mobility, and immediate threats in sparse positions. Identify whether the practical task is to convert, defend, or investigate further.

lessons.name: Trading When Ahead
lessons.objective: Check whether a proposed exchange preserves your advantage.
lessons.overview: Show when exchanging pieces simplifies a win—and when it gives away the advantage. Compare concrete end positions instead of teaching an absolute rule.

lessons.name: Opposition and Move Timing
lessons.objective: Discover how the side to move can change an ending’s outcome.
lessons.overview: Introduce simple positions whose outcome depends on whose turn it is. Play matched examples with the side to move reversed.

lessons.name: Keep a Move in Reserve
lessons.objective: Decide when to spend an extra move to influence the timing.
lessons.overview: Use an available move elsewhere on the board to influence timing. Decide when to spend or preserve that move in a small, verified position.

lessons.name: Coordinate Your Kings
lessons.objective: Use two kings together to reduce an opponent’s escape routes.
lessons.overview: Use two kings to restrict an opponent’s options while protecting one another. Practice reducing escape routes instead of chasing independently.

lessons.name: Finish the Win
lessons.objective: Preserve a winning ending through accurate moves to the finish.
lessons.overview: Convert selected, verified winning endings through capture or immobilization. Focus on preserving the win across several accurate moves.

lessons.name: Save the Draw
lessons.objective: Defend a drawable ending with safe positioning and draw awareness.
lessons.overview: Defend selected drawable endings through safe positioning and avoiding traps. Reinforce repetition and Crown’s implemented draw procedure.

lessons.name: Challenge: Win or Hold
lessons.objective: Convert a winning ending and hold a drawable one.
lessons.overview: Convert one verified winning position and defend one verified drawable position against a suitable response policy. Offer targeted retries from the first consequential mistake.

lessons.name: A Sound Opening
lessons.objective: Develop safely from the starting position with support and mobility.
lessons.overview: Apply safety, support, and mobility from the starting position. Compare early moves by their purpose without requiring named-opening memorization.

lessons.name: Understand Their Last Move
lessons.objective: Identify what your opponent’s last move changed and respond.
lessons.overview: After each opposing move, identify what changed: a threat, an opening, a weakened defender, or a promotion route. Select an appropriate response.

lessons.name: Choose a Plan
lessons.objective: Set a concrete middlegame goal and choose a move that advances it.
lessons.overview: Assess a middlegame position and choose a concrete goal, such as improving a cramped side or preparing a breakthrough. Select a move that advances it.

lessons.name: Know When to Change Plans
lessons.objective: Recognize when an opposing reply calls for a different plan.
lessons.overview: Introduce an opponent’s reply that changes the position. Recognize when an existing plan should be revised or abandoned.

lessons.name: Play with an Advantage
lessons.objective: Continue a favorable position with safe, purposeful play.
lessons.overview: Combine safety, purposeful exchanges, and promotion planning. Continue a favorable middlegame without assuming that every trade is beneficial.

lessons.name: Play from Behind
lessons.objective: Preserve sound resistance, tactical opportunities, and drawing chances.
lessons.overview: Look for sound resistance, tactical opportunities, and drawing chances. Choose moves that preserve possibilities instead of relying on an obvious opponent mistake.

lessons.name: Learn from Your Game
lessons.objective: Review a consequential decision and identify a useful skill to practice.
lessons.overview: Review a short replay, locate a consequential decision, try an improvement, and identify the associated skill. End by selecting a useful practice topic.

lessons.name: Final Challenge: A Complete Game
lessons.objective: Play a complete game, then review and improve several key decisions.
lessons.overview: Play a full game at an appropriate fixed difficulty, then complete a guided review of several decisions. Assess the application of skills and the review—not victory alone.
